lines.text: An ant wanders a prism, one random edge a second. Finish line or trap: which corner comes first?
lines.caption: An ant wanders a prism, one random edge a second. Finish line or trap: which corner comes first?

lines.text: I'm Vantee, and today we're racing an ant to the finish line!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee, and today we're racing an ant to the finish line!

lines.text: A triangular prism has a bottom triangle, A B C, and a top triangle, D E F.
lines.caption: A triangular prism has a bottom triangle, A B C, and a top triangle, D E F.

lines.text: Edges A D, B E and C F join each bottom corner to the one above it.
lines.caption: Edges A D, B E and C F join each bottom corner to the one above it.

lines.text: An ant starts at corner C. Each second, it crawls along one of the three edges at its corner.
lines.caption: An ant starts at corner C. Each second, it crawls along one of the three edges at its corner.

lines.text: All three edges are equally likely. What's the chance it reaches E before it ever reaches A?
lines.caption: All three edges are equally likely. What's the chance it reaches E before it ever reaches A?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's sort out the facts. E is the finish line, and A is the trap.
lines.caption: Let's sort out the facts. E is the finish line, and A is the trap.

lines.text: The walk ends at whichever one the ant reaches first. Sooner or later, it's sure to reach one.
lines.caption: The walk ends at whichever one the ant reaches first. Sooner or later, it's sure to reach one.

lines.text: So we want the chance that E comes first, starting from C.
lines.caption: So we want the chance that E comes first, starting from C.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: a chance for every corner

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: give every corner its own chance of winning.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: give every corner its own chance of winning.

lines.text: From C, call it c. Do the same for B, D and F. E counts as one, and A as zero.
lines.caption: From C, call it c. Do the same for B, D and F. E counts as one, and A as zero.

lines.text: Each neighbor is next with chance one third. So a corner's chance is the average of theirs.
lines.caption: Each neighbor is next with chance one third. So a corner's chance is the average of theirs.

lines.text: B touches A, C and E. So b equals zero plus c plus one, all over three.
lines.caption: B touches A, C and E. So b equals zero plus c plus one, all over three.

lines.text: D touches A, E and F. So d equals zero plus one plus f, all over three.
lines.caption: D touches A, E and F. So d equals zero plus one plus f, all over three.

lines.text: C touches A, B and F. So c equals zero plus b plus f, all over three.
lines.caption: C touches A, B and F. So c equals zero plus b plus f, all over three.

lines.text: F touches C, D and E. So f equals c plus d plus one, all over three.
lines.caption: F touches C, D and E. So f equals c plus d plus one, all over three.

lines.text: Start with the rule at C. Multiply by three: three c equals b plus f.
lines.caption: Start with the rule at C. Multiply by three: three c equals b plus f.

lines.text: Swap in b, then multiply by three again. Nine c equals one plus c plus three f.
lines.caption: Swap in b, then multiply by three again. Nine c equals one plus c plus three f.

lines.text: So eight c equals one plus three f.
lines.caption: So eight c equals one plus three f.

lines.text: The same steps at F, using d, give eight f equals four plus three c.
lines.caption: The same steps at F, using d, give eight f equals four plus three c.

lines.text: Now a neat trick: add them. Eight c plus eight f equals five plus three c plus three f.
lines.caption: Now a neat trick: add them. Eight c plus eight f equals five plus three c plus three f.

lines.text: Take away three c and three f: five c plus five f equals five. So c plus f equals one!
lines.caption: Take away three c and three f: five c plus five f equals five. So c plus f equals one!

lines.text: Then f is one minus c. So eight c equals one plus three minus three c, and eleven c equals four.
lines.caption: Then f is one minus c. So eight c equals one plus three minus three c, and eleven c equals four.

lines.text: So c is four over eleven. That's our answer!
lines.caption: So c is four over eleven. That's our answer!

lines.text: Here's a faster way. That c plus f equals one was no accident.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way. That c plus f equals one was no accident.

lines.text: Look at the front face, A B E D. A and E are opposite corners.
lines.caption: Look at the front face, A B E D. A and E are opposite corners.

lines.text: Push a skewer through the middle of that face, and spin the prism half a turn.
lines.caption: Push a skewer through the middle of that face, and spin the prism half a turn.

lines.text: A and E swap places. So do B and D, and so do C and F. It's the same prism!
lines.caption: A and E swap places. So do B and D, and so do C and F. It's the same prism!

lines.text: So an ant at F racing to E is just like an ant at C racing to A.
lines.caption: So an ant at F racing to E is just like an ant at C racing to A.

lines.text: From C, A comes first with chance one minus c. So f equals one minus c, and d equals one minus b.
lines.caption: From C, A comes first with chance one minus c. So f equals one minus c, and d equals one minus b.

lines.text: Now plug f equals one minus c into our rule from before: eight c equals one plus three f.
lines.caption: Now plug f equals one minus c into our rule from before: eight c equals one plus three f.

lines.text: So eight c equals four minus three c. Eleven c equals four. Four over eleven again!
lines.caption: So eight c equals four minus three c. Eleven c equals four. Four over eleven again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? Whenever a spin swaps the win and the loss. Look for it first.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? Whenever a spin swaps the win and the loss. Look for it first.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers.

lines.text: One third is what you'd get if you guessed b and f are one half each. They aren't.
lines.caption: One third is what you'd get if you guessed b and f are one half each. They aren't.

lines.text: Five over eleven is b, the chance from B. Right work, wrong corner.
lines.caption: Five over eleven is b, the chance from B. Right work, wrong corner.

lines.text: Six over eleven is the chance from D, the letter d. Also the wrong starting corner.
lines.caption: Six over eleven is the chance from D, the letter d. Also the wrong starting corner.

lines.text: Seven over eleven is one minus c, the chance that A comes FIRST. That's the race backwards.
lines.caption: Seven over eleven is one minus c, the chance that A comes FIRST. That's the race backwards.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: a new finish line

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same prism, and the ant starts at C again.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same prism, and the ant starts at C again.

lines.text: Now F is the finish line, and A is still the trap. What's the chance F comes first?
lines.caption: Now F is the finish line, and A is still the trap. What's the chance F comes first?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. A and F are opposite corners of the face A C F D. Skewer it and spin.
lines.caption: Let's check. A and F are opposite corners of the face A C F D. Skewer it and spin.

lines.text: A swaps with F, C with D, and B with E. So e equals one minus b.
lines.caption: A swaps with F, C with D, and B with E. So e equals one minus b.

lines.text: At C: c equals zero plus b plus one, all over three.
lines.caption: At C: c equals zero plus b plus one, all over three.

lines.text: At B: three b equals c plus one minus b, so four b equals c plus one.
lines.caption: At B: three b equals c plus one minus b, so four b equals c plus one.

lines.text: From the C rule, b equals three c minus one. Swap it in: twelve c minus four equals c plus one.
lines.caption: From the C rule, b equals three c minus one. Swap it in: twelve c minus four equals c plus one.

lines.text: So eleven c equals five, and c is five over eleven. If you got it, amazing work!
lines.caption: So eleven c equals five, and c is five over eleven. If you got it, amazing work!

lines.text: Give every corner a chance. Each one is the average of its neighbors' chances.
lines.caption: Give every corner a chance. Each one is the average of its neighbors' chances.

lines.text: Then look for a spin that swaps the win and the loss. Paired chances add up to one.
lines.caption: Then look for a spin that swaps the win and the loss. Paired chances add up to one.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Happy exploring, and see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Happy exploring, and see you next time!
